whatIs: Lenis is a smooth scrolling library: it takes the browser's native scroll and makes it fluid and controllable, with no CSS transforms or replaced scrollbars. You activate it with new Lenis(), it weighs under 5 kB and it supports vertical, horizontal and element-level scrolling.
It's a good fit for brand sites or portfolios where scrolling is part of the experience, especially when you combine it with scroll-linked animations.
uses: Adding smooth scrolling to a portfolio or landing page in React or Vue.
Syncing scroll animations with another library, for example a WebGL scene.
Making anchor links and scrollTo glide with a uniform transition.
caveats: It doesn't work with CSS scroll-snap: to snap to sections you have to use the separate lenis/snap package.
Areas with their own scroll, like a modal or a long menu, need the allowNestedScroll option or the data-lenis-prevent attribute; also, the smoothing doesn't act on iframes.
It's only the scrolling layer: you have to build scroll-reactive animations separately.
pricingNote: Open source under the MIT license; there's only voluntary sponsorship.
idealFor: Sites with polished scrolling in JavaScript, React or Vue.
